about: Hand-curated rules that data/visa-requirements.json does not carry: how days are counted (Schengen, rolling windows, per-entry limits), digital-nomad visas, yellow-fever certificates and tax-residency day tests. Every row has a source link and the date it was checked against that source. Rows are only included where a source was read; a smaller honest file beats a larger guessed one. Rules change: check the linked source before you travel. Not legal or tax advice.

zones.name: Schengen Area
zones.counting: Every day inside the area counts, the entry and exit days included, over any 180-day window ending on the day you check.
zones.freeMovementNote: Citizens of EU and EEA countries and Switzerland move freely and are not held to 90/180.

outside.CY: Cyprus is in the EU but not in the Schengen Area: days there do not count towards Schengen 90/180, and Cyprus counts its own 90 days in 180.
outside.IE: Ireland is in the EU but not in the Schengen Area: days there do not count towards Schengen 90/180.

sources.title: European Commission: Schengen Area (29 countries; Bulgaria and Romania joined on 1 January 2025)

regimes.note: From 15 September 2026 visa-exempt entry is up to 30 days, for tourism. Visa-exempt entry over land borders is normally limited to 2 a calendar year; arrivals by air are not. Reports say 21 nationalities lost visa exemption on the same day and Meridian's dataset predates this, so confirm your passport is still on the list.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Thailand, entry requirements

regimes.note: Entries before 15 September 2026 keep the period granted on arrival (the dataset's figure).

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Thailand, entry requirements

regimes.note: Visa-exempt stays are per entry (45 days for British passports); the exit date is stamped on arrival. An e-visa allows 90 days and multiple entries but only through the entry and exit points chosen on the application.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Vietnam, entry requirements

extension.note: Extendable once, for another 30 days, at an immigration office inside Indonesia, within the first 30 days.

regimes.note: The visa on arrival is single entry, for 30 days.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Indonesia, entry requirements

regimes.note: Georgia lets many passports stay up to one year without a visa (the dataset writes 360 days). Working there, remote work included, needs a work permit since 1 March 2026.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Georgia, entry requirements

regimes.note: Up to 90 days in any 180 for most visa-free passports. The dataset gives some passports (for example the United States) a year; those are counted per entry.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Albania, entry requirements

regimes.note: Up to 90 days in any 180; visits in the previous 180 days count. Montenegro is outside Schengen, so the two counts are separate.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Montenegro, entry requirements

regimes.note: Up to 90 days in any 180 for visa-free passports (stated by FCDO for British citizen passports).

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Turkey, entry requirements

regimes.note: Cyprus counts its own 90 days in 180, apart from Schengen. Time in the north of Cyprus counts towards it.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Cyprus, entry requirements

regimes.note: A Standard Visitor can usually stay up to 6 months a visit (counted here as 180 days), but must not live in the UK through frequent or successive visits.

source.title: GOV.UK: Visit the UK as a Standard Visitor

nomadVisas.name: Telework visa (digital nomad), Spain
nomadVisas.duration: Visa up to 1 year; the residence permit can run up to 3 years.
nomadVisas.income: 200% of Spain's monthly minimum wage (SMI): €2,442 a month for 2026, applying alone; more for family members.
nomadVisas.note: Work for Spanish companies is limited to 20% of your activity. A degree or 3 years' experience is required.
nomadVisas.source: Consulate General of Spain in Washington (Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

nomadVisas.name: Residence or temporary-stay visa for remote work (D8), Portugal
nomadVisas.duration: Temporary stay (up to a year) or residence visa leading to a residence permit.
nomadVisas.income: Average monthly income over the last three months of at least four times Portugal's guaranteed minimum monthly wage.
nomadVisas.note: The page states the rule, not a euro figure; it moves with the minimum wage.
nomadVisas.source: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, consular visa portal

nomadVisas.name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), workcation
nomadVisas.duration: Valid 5 years, multiple entries, 180 days a stay, extendable once by up to 180 days.
nomadVisas.income: Savings of at least 500,000 THB, shown with 3 months of bank statements (a balance requirement, not income).
nomadVisas.note: No Thai work permit, no work for Thai companies or clients.
nomadVisas.source: Royal Thai Embassy, Yangon; requirements also at the Royal Thai Consulate-General, Los Angeles

nomadVisas.name: Digital Nomad Visa, Sri Lanka
nomadVisas.duration: Up to 12 months, renewable each year.
nomadVisas.income: A monthly remittance of at least USD 2,000 for the main applicant (USD 500 more for each dependant beyond two).
nomadVisas.note: Visa fee USD 500 a year per person.
nomadVisas.source: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Sri Lanka

nomadVisas.name: Temporary stay of digital nomads, Croatia
nomadVisas.duration: Up to 18 months; a shorter grant can be extended to 18 months. A new application only 6 months after it ends.
nomadVisas.income: At least €3,622.50 a month, or €43,470 in the bank for 12 months (€65,205 for 18).
nomadVisas.note: No work for employers in Croatia.
nomadVisas.source: Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia

source.title: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1: countries with risk of yellow fever transmission and countries requiring yellow fever vaccination (18 November 2022, revised 3 January 2023)

yellowFever.note: The most recent list WHO publishes. 'from risk countries' means a certificate is asked of travellers arriving from (and for many, transiting through) a country WHO lists as at risk; 'all' means every arriving traveller. Ages are the youngest traveller asked. Requirements change; check with the destination.

taxRules.note: One of the automatic UK tests: 183 or more days in the UK in the tax year (6 April to 5 April). Other tests (home, full-time work, ties) can make you resident with fewer days. HMRC's own day-counting rules are stricter about which days count; Meridian counts every day present.
taxRules.source: GOV.UK (HMRC): Tax on foreign income, residence

taxRules.note: Resident for a year if present more than 183 days, consecutive or not, in any 12-month period starting or ending in that year; or with a home there you seem to intend to keep.
taxRules.source: Portuguese Tax Authority: IRS Code, Article 16

taxRules.note: Tax resident once in New Zealand more than 183 days in any 12-month period; parts of days, such as arrival and departure, count as whole days.
taxRules.source: Inland Revenue (New Zealand): Tax residency status for individuals

taxRules.note: The Sri Lanka digital nomad visa terms say a stay of more than 183 days in any 12 months makes you tax-resident.
taxRules.source: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Sri Lanka

taxDefault.note: Elsewhere Meridian counts days present per calendar year against 183, the common rule of thumb in tax treaties and many national laws. It is a general test, not any one country's rule: your countries' own rules (tax years, homes, centre of interests) decide.

borderRunNotes.note: Visa-exempt entries over land borders are normally limited to 2 a calendar year; immigration may ask frequent visitors for onward travel, accommodation and funds and can refuse entry.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Thailand, entry requirements

borderRunNotes.note: An e-visa obtained inside Vietnam only starts after you leave and re-enter, and only through the entry points named on it.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Vietnam, entry requirements

borderRunNotes.note: Visitors must not live in the UK through frequent or successive visits; a quick exit and return does not restart anything if it looks like living there.

source.title: GOV.UK: Visit the UK as a Standard Visitor

borderRunNotes.note: The 30-day visa on arrival is single entry; leaving ends it.

source.title: UK FCDO travel advice: Indonesia, entry requirements
